results.reader_title: Romanian cities win EU climate recognition despite Romania ranking last on innovation
results.reader_what: Romanian municipalities reached EU Cities Mission status although Romania ranks last on EU innovation and circularity indicators.
results.reader_why: Suggests municipal capacity, not national performance, drives EU framework uptake, with cascade funding as a lever.
results.reader_more: The article asks whether Romanian municipalities can operationalise three EU frameworks: the New European Bauhaus, the Industry 5.0 agenda and the Mission for 100 Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities. It sets published Eurostat and Commission indicators against a case study of the Horizon Europe STARHAUS project, in which Cluj-Napoca is a pilot partner. Romania records the EU's lowest circular material use rate, 1.3 percent in 2024 against an EU average of 12.2 percent, and ranks last on the Summary Innovation Index at 37.7 percent of the EU average, yet three Romanian cities entered the EU Cities Mission. The authors read this decoupling as evidence that municipalities can outperform lagging national systems, and propose a four-layer governance framework. The analysis is desk-based and the case rests on published documentation.

results.reader_more: The paper evaluates the first three years of a Horizon Europe project giving transnational access to research infrastructures for circular economy research. Dedicated support structures consistently lowered access barriers, particularly for less experienced applicants, and the authors argue for centralised support hubs as a coordination mechanism.
